messages:
Maya (Customer): Heads up — after our tenant migration to the org-shared pool, two of our projects started getting 429s even though the project quota tiles on the dashboard show available capacity. Repro steps below.

Maya (Customer): repro: hit /v1/generate with project header X-Project: proj-983, we get 429, body: {"error":"rate_limited"}. Dashboard shows project pool remaining ~120k tokens.

Alex (Support): sorry about that, @Maya. Can you paste the request-id from the 429 response? and which org id this is?

Maya (Customer): request-id: rq_0a9b2c3f, org: org-44. This started after we flipped the tenant to use the new shared-org-pool feature last night. No config changes on client side.

quota-bot: Alert: org-44 rolling-window-exhaustion at 2026-11-04T03:12:09Z - pooled_limit=5e6 tokens, current_consumed=5.1e6 :warning:

Alex (Support): @Jules /eng-ops can you take a look? appears like org pool shows exhausted but project tiles still say available.

Jules (Eng Ops): pulling logs for org-44 and proj-983 now. Quick question: are you using per-project soft-limits or hard caps?

Maya (Customer): hard caps per project, but we expected org pooling to allow burst between projects. Tiles used to show org remaining and project remaining. Now project tiles look stale.

Jules (Eng Ops): got the API logs. I see the 429s come from quota-service with token_bucket:rolled_window_reject. There is a mismatch between meter ledger and dashboard cache. Sample from service log: 
```
[warn] quota_service: reconcile_mismatch org=org-44 project=proj-983 dashboard=120034 ledger=116420 delta=3614
[info] quota_service: accept_window start=2026-11-04T02:00:00Z end=2026-11-04T03:00:00Z bucket_resolution=60s
```
Jules (Eng Ops): dashboard cache shows values computed on tenant-local-time buckets; ledger uses UTC-aligned buckets after the migration. That explains transient tiles that look available while the ledger says exhausted.

Raj (Billing): also seeing invoice-metering lag for org-44. Our billing pipeline uses ledger values (UTC sliding window aggregated) — which is authoritative for enforcement. Dashboards are read from the cache layer which was not migrated to the new bucket alignment.

Maya (Customer): ok — can you confirm if requests are actually being throttled by account-level org pool? We need an ETA to avoid customer impact.

Alex (Support): confirmed — enforcement is at org pool, so 429s are real. Working on mitigation: temporary bump org pool while we fix alignment. @Raj can you approve short bump?

Raj (Billing): approved a 10% emergency bump for org-44 for 1 hour to buy time. I pushed an override: 
```
PATCH /internal/orgs/org-44/pools
body: {"emergency_bump_percent":10, "expires_at":"2026-11-04T04:30:00Z"}
```
Jules (Eng Ops): mitigation in place. Next step: fix dashboard cache alignment. Root cause: rolling-window computation moved to an optimized sliding window service that uses fixed UTC epoch boundaries; dashboard cache still computes per-tenant local bucketing. After migration this divergence surfaced. Fix options: (A) convert dashboard aggregation to use sliding-window from ledger; (B) shift dashboard cache to UTC-aligned buckets; (C) switch enforcement to use tenant-local buckets temporarily — option A preferred.

Alex (Support): estimated timeline for option A?

Jules (Eng Ops): ~4 hours to implement and roll one-way data migration + cache warm. We'll ship a hotfix to compute dashboard aggregates from ledger read API so tiles reflect enforcement numbers.

Maya (Customer): appreciate the quick action. Is there a way for us to detect this client-side earlier?

Jules (Eng Ops): yes: check for monthly/rolling window mismatch by querying enforcement endpoint: 
```
GET /internal/orgs/org-44/enforcement_snapshot?window=1h
Response: {"consumed":5102340, "limit":5000000, "window_start":"2026-11-04T02:12:00Z"}
```
If consumed > dashboard tile remaining -> likely cache misalignment.

Alex (Support): logging action items: 1) keep emergency bump active until patch (Raj) 2) Jules to deploy dashboard->ledger aggregate patch (4h) 3) Support to notify Maya when patch is live + explain root cause 4) Billing to reconcile ledger vs dashboard counts for org-44 for invoice audit.

Raj (Billing): I'll run a reconciliation job comparing ledger and dashboard aggregates for past 7 days and flag any invoice-impacting deltas. Will report back in ~3 hours.

quota-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1104-44 - dashboard/ledger bucket alignment after org-pool migration.

Maya (Customer): thanks all. Please post follow-up when dashboard matches enforcement numbers so we can remove the override. :thumbsup:

Jules (Eng Ops): posting follow-up here when deployed. Quick internal note for postmortem: migration playbook must include bucket-alignment check and a reconciliation run.

Alex (Support): thanks team — keeping this thread open until resolved.
